method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Defines range terms (authorization, range agreement holder, range readiness criteria, riparian area, stream, stubble height) and exempts range holders from Part 4 as needed for Workers Compensation rules.
Prescribes grazing, hay cutting and range developments as range practices.
Applies FRPA s. 112's power to impose conditions to discretions under this regulation.

Lets the minister exempt a range agreement holder from needing a range use or stewardship plan for a set period if grazing will not endanger the range, is in the public interest and is consistent with the objectives.
sections.gapNote: Where grazing proceeds under an exemption there is no range plan for the block review to read; the range-plan rule assumes one exists.

sections.bearsOn: Lists what the minister considers before letting a range holder prepare a range stewardship plan.
Makes ss. 6-11 the government objectives that range use and stewardship plans must address.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for soils: protect soil, minimize erosion, compaction and disturbance, keep protective plant cover and litter, revegetate disturbance.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for forage: healthy plant communities, forage for livestock and wildlife, recruiting desirable plants including by forage seeding, structural variety, litter, and a competitive range industry.
sections.gapNote: Forage seeding on harvested ground (transitory range) competes with reforestation; the crown-grazing pack asks about permanent grazing openings but not about seeding forage on a block.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for water: maintain water resources, healthy riparian and upland areas, and shading riparian vegetation.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for fish: conserve fish, habitat and aquatic ecosystems, and manage deleterious material.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for wildlife: healthy populations and habitat, minimal disturbance in critical periods, and managed predator-livestock interaction.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Sets range plan objectives for biodiversity: conserve it, keep native plant dynamics, encourage late seral communities, and keep successional stages where forage is seeded in transitory range.
sections.gapNote: Transitory range is harvested ground grazed until the new stand closes; the block planner's grazing review could note this objective.

sections.bearsOn: Applies water quality, wildlife habitat area and ungulate winter range objectives to range plans, with Wildlife Act minister exemptions for consistent alternatives.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the minister require a range use plan to contain plant community descriptions and actions, range readiness criteria and stubble heights.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Lets a range stewardship plan propose plant community descriptions, readiness criteria and stubble heights with a rationale, and requires a monitoring and evaluation process.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range plan to specify measures preventing invasive plants spread by range practices.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range stewardship plan holder's grazing schedule to be consistent with the plan.
sections.gapNote: The range-plan rule asks the reviewer to read the plan and its dates; the grazing schedule is where those dates sit for the season of harvest and planting.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the minister require public notice of a range plan, or of a request for a range development authorization, that would materially affect others.
sections.gapNote: A licensee's request to move or rebuild a fence or other range development under FRPA s. 51 may need notice; the range-development rule does not mention it.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a required notice to be followed by at least 30 days' review and comment, consideration of comments, and their submission to the district manager.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the minister set up a range plan advisory committee of at least 3 persons.
Requires a copy of a minor range plan amendment to be given to the district manager.
Lets the minister void a wrongly made minor range plan amendment.

Requires a range plan amendment when an objective is set or changed, the Range Act agreement changes, or the minister gives notice about plant communities, readiness, stubble height or identified issues.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the minister balance objectives and plan content when approving a range plan.
Lets the minister extend a range plan's term if it remains or will be made consistent with objectives and GAR actions.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Repealed; the range of sections holds no text in force.
Bars grazing on Crown range before the plan's range readiness criteria are met, or before the plan's dates unless authorized or readiness is met.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires livestock to be removed at the first of the plan's removal date, its stubble height, or a browse use level (the plan's, else 25% of current annual growth), and grazing not to degrade plant communities.
sections.gapNote: Browse and stubble limits bear on a plantation only indirectly; RPPR s. 44 is the duty the crown-grazing pack tests.

sections.bearsOn: Bars range practices that would materially impair a riparian area's ability to withstand peak flows, filter runoff, store and release water and conserve wildlife habitat.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Bars range practices that would materially and substantially accelerate soil loss, reduce infiltration or moisture storage, or decrease stability on uplands.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices to be timed and done so as to be unlikely to harm fish, fish passage or fish habitat, with ministerial exemptions where impracticable.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices not to deposit harmful material in water diverted for human consumption, nor to damage or destabilize ground round a licensed waterworks.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices to be consistent with a water quality objective from the January after it is set, and livestock to be removed and kept from any part where grazing would be inconsistent with it.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range holder to keep dead livestock 100 m or more from a stream in a community watershed.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices to be consistent with a general wildlife measure (or an approved alternative) from the January after it is set.
sections.gapNote: The UWR and WHA screens cite this for their grazing reach cells.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices to be consistent with a general ecological community measure (or approved alternative) from the January after it is set.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices not to damage or render ineffective a wildlife habitat feature.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires range practices not to damage or render ineffective a resource feature, with exemptions where no other option exists and in the public interest.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Bars the minister from authorizing a range development within 50 m of a stream in a community watershed, or one that would breach the riparian, upland, fish, waterworks, habitat feature or resource feature rules, unless consistent or restored.
sections.gapNote: The range-development rule asks whether the forest work touches a range development; it does not say that a replacement fence or water development is limited by this section.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range agreement holder to keep range developments on its area in effective operating condition, unless exempted.
sections.gapNote: Where harvest damages a fence, the duty to repair it may move to the forest licensee by FRPA s. 51 authorization; the range-development rule covers the authorization.

sections.bearsOn: Requires exposed soil from range development construction to be revegetated with suitable species within 2 years.
sections.gapNote: A range plan duty of the range agreement holder; it bears on a block only where the plan covers the same ground.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range holder to attach livestock tags the minister supplies and report lost tags.
Authorizes cutting Crown timber in the course of a range development authorization or a range plan.
sections.gapNote: Cutting by range holders is outside the cutblock planner.

sections.bearsOn: Requires a range agreement holder who knows grazing will significantly interfere with establishing a free growing stand to remove the livestock and keep them out, unless the minister exempts the second duty once measures prevent recurrence.
Sets the content of intervention orders to range holders and when the holder may recover its costs.
Requires a range stewardship plan holder to report livestock numbers, grazing period and issues each year by 31 December.
Sets how seized livestock may be advertised and sold.

Makes contravening the range practice sections (readiness, removal, riparian, upland, fish, water, GWMs, features, range developments, revegetation, tagging, livestock removal under s. 44, annual reports) an offence up to $5 000 or 6 months; the supplied text also carries the Schedule of range readiness leaf stages.
Gives, for each listed forage species, the leaf stage at which it is ready for grazing, which range readiness under the regulation reads.
sections.gapNote: No rule asks whether livestock turnout waits for the leaf stage of the key forage species; it bears on range use plans, not on a cutblock.
